b644-me-basic-engineering-sciences.baseline_reason: The existing study/source chain covers only a subset of the old TOS Chemistry and Physics topics; close the source/study breadth gap before authoring.
allowed_scope: frequency and period interpretation for a stated periodic process
magnitude and phase interpretation of supplied ideal series resistance and inductive reactance
excluded_scope: general chemistry not represented in the allowed subset
specialist electrical design and component selection
limitations: Author only within the narrow physical-quantity families supported by the linked OpenStax physics and NIST material; do not treat this leaf as a catch-all science category.
The detailed public PRC TOS is Resolution 57 (2013); the 2026 MELE program names only the Mathematics area and does not restate detailed subareas.
b644-me-basic-engineering-sciences.final_reason: A source-traceable, bounded physics/dimensional subset is now covered by the linked study material; chemistry and broader physics remain outside the allowed scope.

b644-me-me-law-code-ethics.baseline_reason: The study material is broad and does not establish complete law/code/ethics coverage; preserve mapped content, but close the study and source traceability gap before authoring.
authorities_verified: R.A. 8495 repeals C.A. 294 as amended by R.A. 5336
Resolution 06 (s. 2003) is reported as the adopted ethics code in secondary copies; official operative text/currentness not verified
allowed_scope: Board, examination, registration, and licensure powers stated in R.A. 8495 and its PRC-linked IRR
statutory practice and equipment definitions under R.A. 8495
the current MELE subject areas/weights and bounded historical TOS crosswalk
excluded_scope: Commonwealth Act 294 / R.A. 5336 provisions repealed by R.A. 8495
detailed ethics canons without a current official code text
technical standards and clause-level obligations not linked by an active PRC source
limitations: PRC currently links R.A. 8495 and Resolution 16 (s. 1998) as the IRR. Board Resolution No. 06 (s. 2003) is identified in secondary copies as an ethics-code adoption, but the current official PRC page supplies no active code text/effectivity record; detailed canons are excluded.
The 2013 detailed TOS remains the last located detailed MELE specification; the 2026 program supplies only the three subject areas and weights.
b644-me-me-law-code-ethics.final_reason: The current official statute, currently PRC-linked IRR, current MELE program, and dedicated legal study material support a narrow statutory/licensure subset; detailed ethics content remains excluded.

b644-me-hvac-refrigeration.baseline_reason: Retain existing bank content and mapped study support; obtain current PRC confirmation of MELE scope before expansion.
authorities_verified: R.A. 8495 practice definition includes HVAC/refrigeration equipment
2025 advanced-PME HVAC specialization is not MELE scope
2024 CPM HVAC TOS is a separate exam regime
allowed_scope: stable refrigeration-cycle and basic HVAC technical principles are study-supported but not authorable until direct MELE scope is confirmed
excluded_scope: all new HVAC/refrigeration question authoring pending direct MELE scope confirmation
refrigerant restrictions, current HVAC codes, fire/life-safety requirements, and specialty certification
limitations: R.A. 8495 defines HVAC/refrigeration equipment and professional practice, but that does not establish MELE exam scope.
The 2024 Certified Plant Mechanic HVAC TOS and 2025 advanced-PME HVAC specialization are different examination/credential regimes and are not used as MELE scope evidence.
The 2026 MELE program does not name HVAC; the publicly located detailed TOS has no explicit HVAC subarea crosswalk for this leaf.
b644-me-hvac-refrigeration.final_reason: Technical study support is sufficient for stable HVAC principles, but the official MELE scope linkage remains materially unresolved.
b644-me-hvac-refrigeration.review_reason: No direct current PRC MELE scope confirmation was found for this BoardPrep-derived HVAC leaf. The professional-practice definition and separate CPM/advanced-PME scope documents cannot substitute for MELE exam-scope evidence.

b644-me-pressure-components.baseline_reason: Official Resolution 57 (2013) separately names thin cylinders, steel tubes, flat plates, and pipe/fittings; present source/study evidence supports only foundational thin-walled cylinder mechanics. Broaden source and study support before future authoring.
allowed_scope: introductory thin-walled cylindrical shell equilibrium and hoop/longitudinal stress with supplied geometry, pressure, material assumptions, and idealization
excluded_scope: pressure-vessel/piping code design, code allowables, joint efficiency, corrosion allowance, certification, and inspection rules
steel-tube, flat-plate, and pipe/fitting design beyond the supported thin-wall cylinder model
limitations: PRC Resolution 57 (2013) names multiple pressure-related subareas, while the technical source supports only introductory thin-walled cylindrical mechanics.
The 2026 program does not restate detailed subareas; no current code-design coverage is inferred.
b644-me-pressure-components.final_reason: MIT OpenCourseWare mechanics and the existing focused study note are sufficient for a limited thin-walled-cylinder subset; unsupported tube/plate/fitting and code design remain excluded.

b644-me-shop-safety-practice.baseline_reason: Existing study notes mention energy isolation but a current authoritative Philippine OSH source is absent.
authorities_verified: PRC MELE subject title includes Shop Practice
allowed_scope: high-level worker information, hazard-reporting, and unsafe-work protections under R.A. 11058 and current D.O. 252-25
isolation, stored-energy control, and verification reasoning when no equipment-specific sequence is inferred
stable shop hazard recognition and general safeguards
excluded_scope: exact lockout/tagout sequence unless supplied by a current applicable procedure
machine-specific guard design and technical standards
numerical penalties, detailed establishment classification, or sector-specific requirements not needed for the scenario
limitations: D.O. 252-25 is the current revised IRR, effective 2025-05-16; prior D.O. 198-18 is superseded.

The public MELE program includes Shop Practice within the 30% subject but does not publish a separate safety subarea; keep authoring at the general shop-practice level and avoid claiming an explicit PRC safety subarea.
b644-me-shop-safety-practice.final_reason: Current DOLE/BWC authority, R.A. 11058, and focused study synthesis support a limited general shop-safety subset with explicit regulatory and procedural exclusions.
